summary: Open source Loom alternative for recording your screen, editing the video and sharing it with a link.
whatItDoes: Cap records your screen, camera and microphone, then lets you share a link or export a finished video. It has a native desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, a web dashboard, and can be fully self-hosted.
problem: Showing your work on video is often faster than another call, but hosted recorders keep your videos on their servers. Cap gives you the same quick share links while letting you choose where recordings are stored.
whoFor: Teams that use Loom and want an open source option
Developers recording bug reports and walkthroughs
Product people making demos and tutorials
Companies that want to self-host their recordings
whyChoose: It is open source and lets you own your storage: use Cap Cloud, your own S3-compatible bucket, keep recordings local, or self-host the whole platform.
requirements: macOS, Windows or Linux for the desktop app
For development: Node.js 24 or newer, Bun 1.4.4, Rust via rustup and Docker
overview: Cap is the open source alternative to Loom. It offers screen recording, local editing, instant share links, comments, transcripts, analytics, team workspaces, custom domains and custom S3 storage.
Instant Mode uploads while you record and gives you a share link as soon as you stop. Studio Mode records locally and opens an editor with backgrounds, zooms, trimming, captions and export controls.
Cap AI can generate titles, summaries, clickable chapters, captions and transcripts, and you can import existing Loom videos into Cap.

features.title: Instant Mode
features.body: Uploads while you record so the share link is ready the moment you stop.

features.title: Studio Mode
features.body: Record locally and edit with backgrounds, zooms, trimming and captions.

features.title: Own your storage
features.body: Use Cap Cloud, connect AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO or Wasabi, or keep recordings local.

features.title: Async feedback
features.body: Comments, reactions, transcripts, viewer analytics and team workspaces.

features.title: Cap AI
features.body: Generates titles, summaries, chapters, captions and transcripts.

features.title: Import from Loom
features.body: Bring existing Loom videos into your Cap library.

strengths: Native desktop app on macOS, Windows and Linux
Password-protected and private shares, custom domains
Open source (AGPLv3, with some crates under MIT)
limitations: Default secrets must be replaced before exposing a self-hosted deployment to the internet
Without email configured, login links only appear in the service logs

useCases.title: Bug reports
useCases.body: Record the bug and send a link instead of writing long steps.

useCases.title: Product demos and tutorials
useCases.body: Record in Studio Mode and polish the video before sharing.

useCases.title: Async standups
useCases.body: Share a quick update and collect comments on the video.

prerequisites: Docker if you want to self-host

steps.title: Download Cap
steps.body: Get Cap for macOS, Windows or Linux from https://cap.so/download

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Sign in or create an account, then choose Instant Mode or Studio Mode.

steps.title: Clone and start
steps.body: Cap will be available at http://localhost:3000.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/CapSoftware/Cap.git
cd Cap
docker compose up -d

steps.title: Find your login link
steps.body: When email is not configured, login links appear in the service logs.

steps.title: Before going public
steps.body: Set public URLs such as CAP_URL and S3_PUBLIC_URL and replace the default secrets. See the self-hosting guide: https://cap.so/docs/self-hosting

steps.title: Point the desktop app at your server
steps.body: In Cap Desktop, set your instance under Settings > Cap Server URL.

environment.name: CAP_URL
environment.description: Public URL of your self-hosted Cap, for production.

environment.name: S3_PUBLIC_URL
environment.description: Public URL of your S3 storage, for production.

firstRun.title: Record your first Cap
firstRun.body: Pick Instant Mode, record, and stop: you get a share link right away. Share the link, export the file, or keep it local.

tutorial.title: Record and share a bug report
tutorial.useCase: You want to show a teammate a bug without scheduling a call.

steps.title: Choose Instant Mode
steps.body: Instant Mode uploads while you record.

steps.title: Record the bug
steps.body: Capture your screen, camera and microphone while you reproduce the problem.

steps.title: Stop and copy the link
steps.body: The share link is ready as soon as you stop recording.

steps.title: Read the feedback
steps.body: Your teammate can comment and react on the video.

tutorial.expected: A shareable link to the recording, with comments and a transcript attached to the video.

costs.label: Software
costs.value: Open source: most code is AGPLv3, some crates are MIT.

costs.label: Cap Cloud
costs.value: Hosted plans are listed on the Cap pricing page; self-hosting is an alternative.

troubleshooting.problem: You can't log in to a self-hosted Cap
troubleshooting.solution: If email isn't configured, read the login link from the logs with docker compose logs cap-web.
